source_notes.finding: GeneralEnv builds user_ns = {tool.name: tool.__call__} for every Tool in its tool set, then adds task.user_ns. Each tool is a plain Python callable in the IPython namespace. There is no generated stub and no schema-to-code step.

The model sees every tool up front. get_toolset_description() writes each tool's signature and description into the prompt as 'Tool function available (already imported in <execute> environment)'. The env passes it into the prompt templates.
No bridge. A tool call is a direct Python call in the same process, inside the IPython shell (P1, P9 with 5 host calls).

None in the executor. PythonREPL is commented 'This PythonREPL is not used by the environment; It is THE ENVIRONMENT' and has no restriction on imports, builtins or files. The NOT_USED signature shows the class is not a tool. The repo's only sandbox language is in mint/utils/exec.py, which is the human-eval correctness harness, and it tells users to sandbox it. The containerized engine is in the chat demo, not the agent environment.

__call__ returns only the captured stdout. An empty output becomes '[Executed Successfully with No Output]'. The traceback path is redacted by regex. The expression value of the last line appears only as an Out line in stdout, so the 2000-char cut can remove it (P2).

Time: timeout=30 by default, enforced by SIGALRM inside time_limit. The shell turns the TimeoutError into text, so the caller gets a string back and no exception (P6). Memory: none. Tool calls: none. The SIGALRM handler needs the main thread (a signal.signal rule), which is inferred from the Python signal docs and not probed.

Persistent for one PythonREPL. reset() calls InteractiveShell.clear_instance() and makes a new shell from a copy of user_ns. GeneralEnv creates one PythonREPL in __init__ (general_env.py:68). The reset() method I read (general_env.py:274-300) does not call python_repl.reset(), so a new episode on the same env object may keep variables. That is inferred from the lines read, not probed (P8 persists in one object).

Exceptions are not raised to the caller. IPython prints a traceback into captured stdout, and the path is redacted. The message and the 'Cell In[1], line N' line both survive (P10). The outer try in handle_tool_call only catches errors from parse_action and the call itself.
None in the code. Anything in the host environment is readable (P5), and a shell command runs with the host's privileges (P12). The repo has no credential handling in this path.

surprises: The 2000-char cut removes the last expression, which is where the return value shows up. A probe that relies on a final-expression result can lose it silently (P2).

The README describes a containerized code execution engine, and that is true for the chat demo. The agent environment that the paper's evaluations use runs PythonREPL in the host process with no container (python_tool.py#L10-L16, general_env.py#L68).
The 30 s limit does work as documented: P6 returned at 30.03 s. It is a SIGALRM inside the shell, so a blocking C call would not be interrupted (not probed).
The memory allocation loop reached 4.14 GB in 0.3 s, which was faster than the 30 s alarm. No memory limit exists below the process's own limits.
The repo's last push was 2024-05-23, so the executor is pinned to an older IPython-era design. The unpinned ipython resolved to 9.18.1.

hardened.config: The repo's containerized code execution engine: JupyterGatewayDocker(name=...) with RESOURCE_CONSTRAINTS {'mem_limit': '8g', 'nano_cpus': 2_000_000_000} (scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py:239-245) and JupyterKernel.execute(code, timeout=60) (scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py:136, 209-213), the same calls api.py:66-90 makes per conversation, documented in README.md:144-150 (https://github.com/xingyaoww/code-act/blob/d607f56c9cfe9e8632ebaf65dcaf2b4b7fe1c6f8/scripts/chat/code_execution/jupyter.py#L239-L245). Image docker.io/xingyaoww/codeact-executor:latest (amd64 only, 7.45 GB compressed, run under emulation). No network option. Harness pins the host port to 41910 and names containers codeact-hardened-<probe>; research/probes/codeact/hardened.py. The in-process PythonREPL's only stricter knob is a lower timeout (python_tool.py:21), which does not change isolation.
